#!/bin/bash
# generic short CPU analysis job: CMD env var = python args (run inside bsccm.sif). 48 cores = full NUMA fraction.
#SBATCH --partition=preempt_cpu
#SBATCH --time=0-02:00:00
#SBATCH -c 48
#SBATCH --mem=120G
#SBATCH -J bsccm_cpu
#SBATCH -o /home/hpc/v181bb/v181bb10/BSCCM/logs/%x_%j.out
set -euo pipefail
cd $HOME/BSCCM
apptainer exec --bind /hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm /hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm/env/bsccm.sif python3 -I $CMD
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# preempt-run.sh [--max N] -- <command...>     run INSIDE an sbatch script (templates/preempt.sbatch)
# Lets a checkpointing job live on the preempt / preempt_cpu partitions. Helma facts (scontrol, 2026-10-24):
# PreemptMode=CANCEL (a preempted job is killed, NEVER requeued), GraceTime=900 s from SIGTERM to SIGKILL,
# PreemptExemptTime=2 h (not preempted in its first 2 h), MaxNodes=1, MaxTime=2 days, DefaultTime=10 min.
# On SIGTERM (preemption, scancel) or SIGUSR1 (`#SBATCH --signal=B:USR1@900` = 15 min before the wall time):
#   1. resubmits the batch script saved at the chain's first start, held until this job ends (afterany),
#      with this job's environment + PREEMPT_ROOT/PREEMPT_RESUBMITS (sbatch command-line options and
#      positional args are NOT replayed: put every option in #SBATCH lines, parameters in env vars);
#   2. passes ONE SIGTERM to the command (Slurm signals only this batch shell, measured 2026-10-30); it must checkpoint + exit;
#   3. waits for it. The successor must resume from the latest checkpoint by itself (e.g. --resume auto).
# The command exiting on its own = no resubmit; after a signal, rc other than 0/143 cancels the successor.
# A successor of a run that had already finished must exit at once (resume sees training complete).
# Chain records, ~/.claude/state/preempt-chain/: <job>.info, <job>.next (successor; wait-job.sh follows it),
# <root>.sbatch (the replayed script), stop-<root> (no more resubmits; written by preempt-cancel.sh).
# A plain `scancel` also sends SIGTERM and WOULD resubmit -- cancel a chain with bin/preempt-cancel.sh.
set -uo pipefail
MAX=${PREEMPT_MAX:-20}
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do case "$1" in --max) MAX="$2"; shift 2;; --) shift; break;; *) break;; esac; done
[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: preempt-run.sh [--max N] -- <command...>" >&2; exit 64; }
if [ -z "${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}" ]; then echo "preempt-run.sh: not in a SLURM job, running plainly" >&2; exec "$@"; fi
C="$HOME/.claude/state/preempt-chain"; mkdir -p "$C"
find "$C" -type f -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null   # housekeeping: chains older than a month
J=$SLURM_JOB_ID; ROOT=${PREEMPT_ROOT:-$J}; PR_LINK=${PREEMPT_RESUBMITS:-0}  # not "N": an exported job parameter N would be overwritten for the child (Cress 2026-11-09: cascades ran with N=0)
log(){ echo "[preempt-run $(date +%H:%M:%S) job $J] $*"; }
[ -s "$C/$ROOT.sbatch" ] || scontrol write batch_script "$J" "$C/$ROOT.sbatch" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || log "WARNING: could not save the batch script - resubmission will fail"
printf 'root=%s link=%s node=%s start=%s\n' "$ROOT" "$PR_LINK" "$(hostname)" "$(date +%FT%T)" > "$C/$J.info"
log "link $PR_LINK of chain $ROOT (max $MAX resubmits)"

[ -e "$C/stop-$ROOT" ] && { log "stop-$ROOT present: chain stopped, not running"; exit 0; }
child=""; sig=""; resub=0; busy=0
resubmit(){
  [ "$resub" -eq 1 ] || [ "$busy" -eq 1 ] && return; busy=1   # once per job; a failed submit is retried on the next signal
  if [ -e "$C/stop-$ROOT" ]; then log "$1: stop-$ROOT present, not resubmitting"; return; fi
  if [ "$PR_LINK" -ge "$MAX" ]; then log "$1: $MAX resubmits reached, not resubmitting"; return; fi
  local unset=() v out err
  for v in $(compgen -e | grep -E '^(SLURM|SBATCH)_'); do unset+=(-u "$v"); done   # no job env leaking into sbatch
  err=$(mktemp); out=$(cd "${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}" && env "${unset[@]}" PREEMPT_ROOT="$ROOT" PREEMPT_RESUBMITS=$((PR_LINK+1)) \
        sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterany:"$J" --export=ALL "$C/$ROOT.sbatch" 2>"$err")
  if [[ "$out" =~ ^([0-9]+) ]]; then
    echo "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" > "$C/$J.next"; resub=1; log "$1: resubmitted as ${BASH_REMATCH[1]} (starts after $J ends)"
    [ -e "$C/stop-$ROOT" ] && { scancel "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" 2>/dev/null; log "stop arrived during submit: cancelled ${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; }
  else log "$1: RESUBMIT FAILED: $out $(cat "$err")"; fi
  rm -f "$err"; busy=0
}
# Both SIGTERM and SIGUSR1 are passed on to the command as ONE SIGTERM. Measured on Helma 2026-10-30 (MicroGreens probe): a
# plain scancel signals ONLY this batch shell - the command never heard it and was SIGKILLed after KillWait (30 s) - and
# --signal=B:USR1 also reaches only this shell. A command that Slurm signalled directly as well gets a duplicate SIGTERM.
fwd=0
on_sig(){ sig=$1; log "got SIG$1"; resubmit "SIG$1"
  [ "$fwd" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$child" ] && { fwd=1; kill -TERM "$child" 2>/dev/null; log "passed SIGTERM to the command (pid $child)"; }; }
trap 'on_sig TERM' TERM; trap 'on_sig USR1' USR1
[ -n "$sig" ] && { log "SIG$sig before launch: not starting (successor continues)"; exit 0; }
"$@" & child=$!
[ -n "$sig" ] && [ "$fwd" -eq 0 ] && { fwd=1; kill -TERM "$child" 2>/dev/null; }   # signal between the check and the launch
while kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; do wait "$child"; done
wait "$child"; rc=$?
log "command exited rc=$rc${sig:+ after SIG$sig}"
if [ -n "$sig" ] && [ -e "$C/$J.next" ]; then
  case "$rc" in 0|143) exit 0;; esac                  # checkpointed and stopped: the successor continues
  nx=$(cat "$C/$J.next")
  if scancel "$nx" 2>/dev/null; then rm -f "$C/$J.next"; log "command FAILED (rc=$rc) after SIG$sig: cancelled successor $nx"
  else log "command FAILED (rc=$rc) after SIG$sig: could NOT cancel successor $nx - run preempt-cancel.sh $J"; fi
fi
exit "$rc"

"""BSCCM training-format access (pack = fixed-record .npy memmaps, row = global_index).
  led_array (N,23,128,128) u2 | fluor (N,6,128,128) u2 [NEVER an LF input: contains the marker signal] | dpc (N,128,128) f4 (quantitative phase, rad)
  histology (Nh,398,398,3) u2 (rows via targets_v2['hist_row'])
LF normalisation v2 (N005): ratio = (raw-30)/(bg_p50 crop at the cell's FOV position - 30); x = log(ratio / slide_scale[slide,c]) / s_c.
Phase channel appended (optional): dpc / 1.0 rad."""
import numpy as np, torch
W = '/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm'
LED = ["Brightfield","DF_50","DF_50_Bottom","DF_50_Right","DF_55","DF_60","DF_60_Bottom","DF_60_Right","DF_65","DF_70","DF_70_Bottom","DF_70_Right","DF_75","DF_80","DF_80_Bottom","DF_80_Right","DF_85","DF_90","DPC_Bottom","DPC_Left","DPC_Right","DPC_Top","LED119"]
CHSETS = {'all': list(range(23)), 'bf': [0], 'dpc4': [18, 19, 20, 21], 'bf_dpc4': [0, 18, 19, 20, 21], 'df': list(range(1, 18)), 'no119': list(range(22)),
          'none': [], 'df_low': list(range(1, 9)), 'df_high': list(range(9, 18)), 'led119': [22]}
def chan_list(spec):
    if spec in CHSETS: return CHSETS[spec]
    if '+' in spec: return sorted({c for part in spec.split('+') for c in chan_list(part)})   # e.g. bf+dpc4
    return [int(c) for c in spec.split(',')]
class LFNorm:
    def __init__(s, pack=W + '/pack'):
        s.pack = pack; s.led = None
        meta = np.load(W + '/cellmeta.npz'); s.py, s.px, s.slide = meta['pos_y'], meta['pos_x'], meta['slide']
        n = np.load(W + '/led_norm.npz'); s.scale, s.s_c = n['slide_scale'], n['s_c']
    def _open(s):
        if s.led is None:
            s.led = np.load(s.pack + '/led_array.npy', mmap_mode='r'); s.bg = np.load(W + '/backgrounds_p50.npy', mmap_mode='r'); s.dpc = np.load(s.pack + '/dpc.npy', mmap_mode='r')
    def __call__(s, g, ch, phase=False):
        s._open(); H = s.bg.shape[1]; y0, x0 = int(s.py[g]) - 64, int(s.px[g]) - 64
        ya, yb, xa, xb = max(y0, 0), min(y0 + 128, H), max(x0, 0), min(x0 + 128, H)
        b = np.asarray(s.bg[:, ya:yb, xa:xb][ch], np.float32)          # slice the 128x128 window FIRST (cheap), then channels
        if b.shape[1:] != (128, 128):                                   # cells near the FOV edge: edge-pad the flat field
            b = np.pad(b, ((0, 0), (ya - y0, y0 + 128 - yb), (xa - x0, x0 + 128 - xb)), mode='edge')
        raw = np.asarray(s.led[g][ch], np.float32)
        r = (raw - 30) / (b - 30) / s.scale[s.slide[g], ch][:, None, None]
        x = np.log(np.clip(r, 1e-3, None)) / s.s_c[ch][:, None, None]
        if phase: x = np.concatenate([x, np.asarray(s.dpc[g], np.float32)[None]], 0)
        return x
class CellSet(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    """LF image (+ optional phase) -> marker targets/masks (targets_v2), class labels, global row."""
    def __init__(s, rows, channels='all', phase=True, train=False, targets=W + '/targets_v3.npz'):
        s.rows = np.asarray(rows); s.ch = chan_list(channels); s.phase = phase; s.train = train; s.norm = LFNorm()
        T = np.load(targets); s.Y, s.M, s.c3, s.c10 = T['Y'], T['mask'], T['cls3'], T['cls10']
    def __len__(s): return len(s.rows)
    def __getitem__(s, i):
        g = int(s.rows[i]); x = torch.from_numpy(s.norm(g, s.ch, s.phase))
        if s.train:   # NO rotations/flips: DPC_Left/Right/Top/Bottom and DF_*_Bottom/_Right are direction-specific, so a rotation
            # would silently relabel illumination directions. Only small translations (cells are centred +- detection error).
            dy, dx = np.random.randint(-4, 5, 2); x = torch.roll(x, (int(dy), int(dx)), (1, 2))
        return x, torch.from_numpy(s.Y[g]), torch.from_numpy(s.M[g]), int(s.c3[g]), int(s.c10[g]), g
"""Extract the 50th-percentile flat-field backgrounds (one per LED channel, 2056x2056) -> backgrounds_p50.npy (23,2056,2056) f4, LED order."""
import zarr, numpy as np, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/home/hpc/v181bb/v181bb10/BSCCM'); from bsccm.data import LED
W='/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm'
s=zarr.storage.ZipStore(W+'/BSCCM.zarr.zip',mode='r'); g=zarr.open_group(s,mode='r',path='BSCCM/BSCCM_backgrounds.zarr')
out=np.stack([np.asarray(g[c]['50_percentile'][:],dtype=np.float32) for c in LED])
np.save(W+'/backgrounds_p50.npy',out); print(out.shape, [round(float(np.median(o)),1) for o in out])

import os as _os; CLEAN = _os.environ.get('BSCCM_CLEAN', '0') == '1'; S_ = 'c' if CLEAN else ''
CF = _os.environ.get('BSCCM_COFACTOR', 'q10'); TAG = '' if CF == 'q10' else (_os.environ['BSCCM_TAG'] if CF.startswith('map:') else f'_cf{CF}')

Labels only; no images/predictions. All fits use same-draw split-0 hist_row<0.
Fit XS=(total-background_lowess)/shading above BOTH released marker/autofluor
floors, then assess the floor-clipped six-channel affine prediction on ALL clean
split-0 cells. Floors identify censored/nonnegative-unmixing boundary regimes;
the autofluor value is never a predictor of the new raw label. If r>=.99, apply
exactly that map/floor to XL=(total-background)/shading.

Predeclared fallback if r<.99: spectral least squares using positive-gate minus
other-cell XL mean (clipped nonnegative, unit norm), plus same-draw unstained XL
mean and two centered PCs. All references use clean split-0 only. Project XL on
the basis pseudoinverse; subtract its split-0 0.5th percentile and floor
at a tiny positive split-0 scale for positive-q10 v3 compatibility. Fallback is not used on current data; no downstream QC chooses it.
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

CHANNELS = ['426-446', '500-550', '550-570', '585-625', '627-673', '690-']
MARKERS = ['CD45', 'CD123', 'CD19', 'CD56', 'CD14', 'CD16', 'HLA-DR', 'CD3']


def corr(a, b):
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])


def channels(sm, background):
    x = np.column_stack([
        (sm[f'Fluor_{c}_total_raw'] - sm[f'Fluor_{c}_{background}']) /
        sm[f'Fluor_{c}_shading'] for c in CHANNELS]).astype(float)
    if not np.isfinite(x).all():
        raise ValueError('Non-finite channels or invalid shading')
    return x


def derive(source, out):
    source, out = Path(source), Path(out)
    if source.resolve() == out.resolve():
        raise ValueError('Output must be separate from read-only source')
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    sm = pd.read_parquet(source / 'bsccm_sm.parquet')
    idx = pd.read_parquet(source / 'bsccm_index.parquet')
    with np.load(source / 'targets.npz') as t:
        cal = (t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0)
    assert len(idx) == len(sm) == len(cal)
    assert np.array_equal(idx.global_index.to_numpy(), np.arange(len(idx)))
    xs, xl = channels(sm, 'background_lowess'), channels(sm, 'background')
    zs = np.column_stack([xs, np.ones(len(xs))])
    zl = np.column_stack([xl, np.ones(len(xl))])
    af = sm.autofluor_single_antibody_model_unmixed.to_numpy()
    ab, batch = idx.antibodies.to_numpy(), idx.batch.to_numpy()
    result = pd.DataFrame(index=sm.index)
    records, models = [], {}
    for m in MARKERS:
        col = f'{m}_single_antibody_model_unmixed'
        y = sm[col].to_numpy()
        value = y.copy()  # v3 never consumes unmeasured rows
        for b in (0, 1):
            slide = (ab == m) & (batch == b)
            tr = slide & cal
            floor, af_floor = float(y[tr].min()), float(af[tr].min())
            interior = tr & (y > floor * (1 + 1e-6)) & (af > af_floor * (1 + 1e-6))
            if interior.sum() < 50:
                raise ValueError(f'Too few interior cells: {m}, draw {b}')
            coef = np.linalg.lstsq(zs[interior], y[interior], rcond=None)[0]
            pred = np.maximum(floor, zs[tr] @ coef)
            r = corr(y[tr], pred)
            rec = dict(target=m, draw=b, n_cal=int(tr.sum()), n_fit=int(interior.sum()),
                       floor=floor, r=r, residual_sd=float(np.std(y[tr] - pred)),
                       target_sd=float(np.std(y[tr])),
                       floor_fraction=float(np.mean(y[tr] == floor)))
            # Also report the requested plain linear tests with/without autofluor.
            for key, z in [('ols6', zs), ('ols6_af', np.column_stack([xs, af, np.ones(len(xs))]))]:
                c = np.linalg.lstsq(z[tr], y[tr], rcond=None)[0]
                p = z[tr] @ c
                rec[key + '_r'] = corr(y[tr], p)
                rec[key + '_residual_sd'] = float(np.std(y[tr] - p))
            model = dict(coef=coef.tolist(), floor=floor, method='recovered_clipped_affine')
            if r >= .99:
                value[slide] = np.maximum(floor, zl[slide] @ coef)
            else:
                g = sm[f'selection_example_{m}_positive_cells_batch_{b}'].to_numpy().astype(bool)
                unst = (ab == 'unstained') & (batch == b) & cal
                if min((tr & g).sum(), (tr & ~g).sum(), unst.sum()) < 3:
                    raise ValueError('Too few spectral-reference cells')
                dye = np.maximum(xl[tr & g].mean(0) - xl[tr & ~g].mean(0), 0)
                dye /= np.linalg.norm(dye)
                mu = xl[unst].mean(0)
                pcs = np.linalg.svd(xl[unst] - mu, full_matrices=False)[2][:2]
                basis = np.column_stack([dye, mu / np.linalg.norm(mu), pcs.T])
                a = xl[slide] @ np.linalg.pinv(basis)[0]
                atr = a[cal[slide]]
                offset = float(np.percentile(atr, .5))
                local_floor = float(max(np.median(np.abs(atr)) * 1e-6, 1e-12))
                value[slide] = np.maximum(local_floor, a - offset)
                model = dict(method='spectral_ls_fallback', basis=basis.tolist(),
                             offset=offset, floor=local_floor)
            rec['method'] = model['method']
            records.append(rec)
            models[f'{m}|b{b}'] = model
            print(f'{m} draw {b}: r={r:.9f}, residual_sd={rec["residual_sd"]:.6g}, {rec["method"]}', flush=True)
        result[col] = value
    result.to_parquet(out / 'raw_v8.parquet', index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(records).to_csv(out / 'unmixing_fidelity.csv', index=False)
    (out / 'unmixing_maps.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(
        channels=CHANNELS, fit='same-draw split-0 hist_row<0; exclude both floors',
        fidelity='all same-draw clean split-0 single-antibody cells', models=models), indent=2) + '\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument('--source', default='/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm')
    ap.add_argument('--out', required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    derive(args.source, args.out)

**Decision: FAIL; stop before stage 2. No LF model was trained or scored on v8; no prediction files were loaded.**

Recovered the authors’ single-antibody unmixing separately for eight markers × two draws, using only same-draw split-0 cells with hist_row<0. XS=(total_raw−background_lowess)/shading; XL=(total_raw−background)/shading over the six specified channels. The released outputs have floors and nonnegative-unmixing boundary regimes. I fitted a six-channel affine map on cells above both marker and autofluor floors, and restored the split-0 marker floor when assessing fidelity on **all** clean split-0 cells. The v8 raw label applies that exact clipped map to XL. The autofluor column only identifies interior calibration cells; its released values are never an input to the new raw prediction.

Plain OLS tests are also in `unmixing_fidelity.csv`: six channels alone have minimum r=0.978174 (CD19 draw 0), and adding released autofluor gives r≥0.999579. Evaluate each marker and direction separately; an overall refutation requires both markers in both directions. A result above 0.72 alone does not establish reachability.

Local-background reconstruction differs from the authors’ smoothed background and is audited against released intensities. The Spearman–Brown interpretation assumes equivalent halves and independent errors; clipping/asinh and checkerboard spatial structure make this approximate.

Unstained spread is a diagnostic containing autofluorescence and biological variation, not pure instrumental variance. FOV residual share is a descriptive variance decomposition of y minus the specified three-model ensemble; it also includes model error and FOV cell-composition differences, and is not a causal label-error estimate.

Scope: answer 9 data questions from the paper, the official repo, the Dryad page, and a few read-only checks on our local copy. ## Sources and how they were read | Tag | Source | Notes | |---|---|---| | **[P]** | Pinkard, Liu, Nyatigo, Fletcher, Waller, "The Berkeley Single Cell Computational Microscopy (BSCCM) Dataset", arXiv:2402.06191 **v1** (9 Feb 2024). HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/2402.06191v1 ; PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.06191 | Only v1 exists (`/html/...v2` and `v3` return 404, and the abs page lists only [v1]). Cited by section name (e.g. [P §S1.1 "Histology staining"]). The figure PNGs (Fig S2, S4, S5, Fig 3) were looked at directly (https://arxiv.org/html/2402.06191v1/data_processing.png, `cell_type_clustering.png`, `demixing_details.png`, `bsccm_led_array_patterns.png`). | | **[R]** | https://github.com/Waller-Lab/BSCCM at commit `64de2e0f681a09be3f2a91ae4ead27628bab353d` (shallow clone, since deleted) | `.py` files are cited by line number. Notebooks are cited as `file.ipynb` JSON line N (the line in the raw .ipynb file) or "cell k" (0-based code/markdown cell index). | | **[D]** | Dryad record https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.sxksn038s (landing page read with WebFetch) | Versions: 2024-02-08 initial; 2025-05-06 "fixed a bug in the BSCCM-tiny metadata". The page lists no known issues and no donor/IRB text. | | **[L]** | Read-only checks on our local copy (`/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm/`: `bsccm_index.parquet`, `bsccm_sm.parquet`, `BSCCM.zarr.zip`, `pack/*.npy`) | Scripts are in this session's scratchpad (not the repo). The numbers below were measured first-hand. | | **[G]** | Getting_started.ipynb in [R] | The official tutorial. | | **[I]** | Pinkard et al., "Information-driven design of imaging systems", arXiv:2405.20559v4 (https://arxiv.org/html/2405.20559v4) | A downstream use of BSCCM by the same first author. | Not reachable: H. Pinkard's PhD thesis "Data-Driven Information-Optimal Computational Microscopy" (UC Berkeley 2022, https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0kw136nx). [P §S1.1] calls the autofocus "described in full in chapter 2", so the paper was adapted from this thesis. eScholarship serves a bot check, so it was not read. It may hold donor and batch details that the paper leaves out **[unverified]**. --- ## Q1. Histology: acquisition, matching, mismatch rate, why only unstained, which stain **Acquisition (same slide, stained after LED imaging):** yes. - The imaging chamber was designed to "be disassembled so that a subsequent histology staining step could be applied, without moving cells" [P §S1.1 "Assembling imaging chambers"]. It is a poly-L-lysine coverslip with a 600 µm acrylic spacer, waxed to a slide. Cells were fixed to the coverslip with 4 rounds of 16% PFA exchange [P §S1.1 "Filling imaging chambers with cells"]. - "After imaging in fluorescence and LED-array modes, **some chambers** were disassembled for histology staining" [P §S1.1 "Histology staining"]. The chamber was opened under water and the coverslip released with a razor blade. The epoxy-sealed end was cut off with a diamond knife. The coverslip was stained 1 min in **Wright's stain (Sigma-Aldrich #45253)**, then dipped 5x in 25% ethanol phosphate buffer at pH 6.65 and 2x in low-concentration phosphate buffer at pH 6.65. It was blotted, dried overnight, scraped of wax, mounted in Neo-Mount on a **fresh slide**, and cleaned with methanol. - Why a separate step: "having a histology stain on the cells during imaging with the LED array would alter their absorption/scattering properties, and could potentially alter the fluorescence signal as well" [P §S1.1 "Histology staining"]. - Imaging: Zeiss Axio Observer, **63x 1.4 NA oil** objective, the same monochrome Basler acA2440-75um camera. RGB was formed by lighting the **red, green and blue brightfield LEDs of the same LED array one after another** [P §3 ¶2; §S1.1 "Microscope and data collection"]. - Autofocus was not the single-shot method. Focal stacks were taken at a subset of XY positions, and a running average interpolated the focus offset elsewhere [P §S1.1]. - Global metadata [L, `BSCCM/BSCCM_global_metadata.json` extracted from the zip]: histology `pixel_size_um` 0.0534, image_shape 398x398, channel_names [Red, Green, Blue], wavelengths 630/515/460 nm, exposures R55/G60/B70 ms, camera offset 30, gain 0 dB (the LED/fluor gain is 4 dB). - **398 px x 0.0534 µm = 21.25 µm, which equals the LED crop's 128 px x 0.166 µm = 21.25 µm.** The two crops cover the same physical field of view, which matters for registration. - Bit depth: histology is stored as uint16 holding 12-bit values per channel ("398x398 36-bit") [P Table 1]. `read_image(..., 'histology')` divides by 2^12 by default (`convert_histology_rgb32`) [R `bsccm/bsccm.py` L257-258]. The docstring says "10-bits per pixel" (L214-215), which contradicts the code; the 2^12 divisor and "36-bit" agree with each other. **Stain: Wright's, not Giemsa.** - The paper gives Wright's three times, with a catalog number: [P §3 ¶2], [P Fig S1e caption], and [P §S1.1 "Histology staining"] ("Wright's stain (Sigma-Aldrich # 45253)"). Sigma 45253 is "Wright's stain solution for microscopy" (eosin Y + polychromed methylene blue; https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/product/sigma/45253). - The tutorial alone says "Histology, Which are **Giemsa** stained cells" [G JSON L260]. Treat that as a documentation slip. Both are Romanowsky-type stains, so they look similar, but the paper's protocol with a catalog number takes precedence. **Registration / matching method** [P §S1.2, last two paragraphs; Fig S2i]: 1. Histology cells were detected with a difference-of-Gaussians blob finder. Candidates with a low summed gradient (out-of-focus or empty crops) were removed. "This was the only exclusion step needed". 2. **One global rigid transform per slide** (translation + rotation, no scale, no local warp). It was fitted by grid search on the GPU (JAX), minimising the sum over histology cells of the distance to the nearest LED/fluor cell, and "confirmed by looking at the visual alignment" (Fig S2i). 3. Matching is then nearest-neighbour, described as "one-to-one matching of histology cell candidates to LED array/fluorescence ones". The LED/fluor cells had already passed the CNN QC filter, so a histology crop only exists for cells that survived that filter. **Expected mismatch rate:** **not reported anywhere** [P], [R], [D]. - No per-pair distance threshold, residual statistics, or match fraction is given. The code that did the matching is **not in the repo**: grep finds no histology alignment code; `bsccm/creation/` holds only crop/tiny/upload notebooks [R]. - Risk factors that follow from the method [inference]: - Cells can be lost or shifted during disassembly, staining, and remounting on a new slide. - A single rigid transform cannot absorb local stage nonlinearity over a full slide scan (~16 h, several mm). - Density-dependent nearest-neighbour ambiguity. - Different objectives and focus. - Fig S2i shows qDPC detections without a histology partner, so cell loss certainly happens. The fraction is not quantified [unverified]. - **Recommendation:** measure it ourselves (e.g. nuclear-mask or phase-vs-absorbance correlation per pair, flagging low-similarity pairs). The physical FOVs match (21.25 µm), so a centred-crop similarity score is meaningful. **Why only unstained cells?** The paper never says so explicitly. It only says "some chambers" were stained, and the Getting_started tutorial says "a small subset" [G JSON L260]. Our data shows all 15,712 histology-matched cells are `antibodies=='unstained'` (verified upstream by the caller and re-checked below). Plausible reasons [inference, not stated by authors]: - The stain could alter or quench fluorescence. The authors note it "could potentially alter the fluorescence signal". - Unstained slides were the expendable controls. The antibody slides were the more valuable fluorescence measurements and were not disassembled. The consequence for us: **no cell has histology + surface-marker labels together** (unstained cells have autofluorescence only). Histology and marker targets can only be linked through the label-free images. Histology availability by slide [L] (appendix A4): - Only **two slides** were histology-stained, both unstained (no-antibody) slides: **(batch 0, rep 0): 10,015 of 16,338 cells matched (61%)** and **(batch 1, rep 1): 5,697 of 14,055 (41%)**. The other unstained slide, (b1, rep 0) with 32,674 cells, has none. - So **39-59% of the LED cells on a stained slide got no histology partner**. That is the observable non-match rate. - **First-hand split by FOV [L]:** - On (b0, rep0), 484 of 3,258 FOVs (15%) have zero matches and hold 27% of the unmatched cells. The matched FOVs stop at stage y ≤ 46,150 µm while LED FOVs reach 49,282 µm. - On (b1, rep1), 1,372 of 3,334 FOVs (41%) have zero matches and hold 65% of the unmatched cells. Matched FOVs stop at y ≤ 40,630 µm while LED FOVs reach 50,062 µm. - **So a large part of the non-matching is incomplete histology scan coverage (a missing slide region)**, especially in batch 1. - **Within FOVs that do have matches, only 68% (b0) / 66% (b1) of cells are matched.** That ~1/3 per-cell loss is from cell detachment during staining, the gradient focus filter, and/or matching failure. - The match rate does not depend on in-FOV radius (0.61-0.62 b0, 0.40-0.42 b1 across radius bins). - The rate of *wrong* matches among the 15,712 pairs is unknown. A ~1/3 per-cell loss in covered FOVs means nearest-neighbour matching sometimes had missing partners. **A wrong-neighbour match is plausible wherever a cell's true partner was lost but a neighbour lies close by** [inference], so a per-pair similarity QC is advisable. - The b1 histology slide is also the one imaged **without the camera ROI** [P §S1.5], so its FOV geometry differs from all other slides. ## Q2. What is the `dpc` array? **Quantitative phase (qDPC) reconstructed from the 4 half-annulus DPC images. It is not a raw DPC difference image.** - [P §S2 "BSCCM_images.zarr"]: `"dpc": Quantitative differential phase contrast images (which were computed from raw DPC led-array images)`. - [P §S1.2]: "the 4 differential phase contrast (DPC) images at each field of view were used as input to an inverse algorithm that computed quantitative phase [23] (qDPC)". Ref [23] is Tian & Waller, "Quantitative differential phase contrast imaging in an LED array microscope", Opt. Express 23:11394 (2015). That algorithm is a weak-object transfer function (WOTF) model with an L2/Tikhonov-regularised closed-form deconvolution. - **It was computed per full field of view (2056x2056) and then cropped**: "qDPC images were calculated for each field of view" [P Fig S2c caption]. It was also used for blob detection and as one input to the QC CNN [P §S1.2]. A crop of a full-FOV reconstruction differs from a reconstruction of the 128x128 crop (boundary/low-frequency behaviour). - dtype float32 [G cell 17; L zarr meta `dpc` `/

_percentile`, p ∈ {5, 10, 20, 40, 50}; - each array is **float64, shape (2056, 2056) = the full camera FOV**, chunks (257, 514). - There is **one array per LED channel**, including `LED119`, and it is **not per slide or per batch**: the group has no slide/batch level. - There are **no fluorescence or DPC backgrounds** in this zarr (only LED channel names appear). - The docstring of `get_background` says "specific to each physical slide" [R `bsccm.py` L344-351], but the code indexes only `[channel]['{p}_percentile']` and crops 128x128 around the cell's `position_in_fov_{x,y}_pix` (L358-362). **So it is one global flat field per channel; the "per slide" docstring is wrong** (verified from the zarr layout). - It is absent from the tiny and MNIST variants (warning in `bsccm.py` L352-353; GitHub issue #6). - Edge case: crops for cells within 64 px of the FOV border are truncated by the slicing in L361 (no padding). Cell positions span x 52-1967 and y 180-1916 [L], so a few cells near x < 64 get a background crop narrower than 128 px. **Recommended LED normalisation (the authors' own recipe):** - Shading correction is "raw measurements ... divided by an image taken on the same system under the same illumination, but without a sample" [P §2.1]. - The concrete form in the tutorial is `(raw - offset) / (background_p50 - offset)` with `offset = 30` [G cell 57, JSON L1786, L1804-1805]. The camera offset is 30 for LED, fluor and histology in global metadata [L]. - Caveat [P §S1.5, last bullet]: "From slide-to-slide and batch-to-batch, there are variations in the average intensity of images in a given channel ... the LED119 channel ... has very different average brightness between batch 0 and batch 1." - A single global flat field cannot remove per-slide gain differences. - Add a per-slide (batch x antibodies x slide_replicate) per-channel intensity normalisation (e.g. divide by the slide's median of background-region pixels), or at least evaluate across batches [recommendation]. - Exposures differ by channel: Brightfield 8 ms; DF_50 29 ms ... It used 15 train-test splits for information estimates. This is consistent with using the per-condition single-antibody targets with masking. The exact columns and normalisation were not visible in the parts read [unverified]. - **Recommendation for N003:** define our own splits. - (i) A random within-batch split for development. - (ii) **Batch-held-out** (train b0 → test b1 and vice versa) as the primary generalisation test. - (iii) Ideally slide-level held-out within batch, to separate slide/imaging-date effects.  fluor_dataframe = pd.DataFrame()
# copy over global insex
fluor_dataframe.insert(0, 'global_index', dataset.index_dataframe.global_index.to_list())

for index in dataset.index_dataframe.global_index:
    index = int(index)
    print('{}          \r'.format(index), end='')

    for ch_index, fluor_channel in enumerate(dataset.global_metadata['fluorescence']['channel_names']):    
        #compute fluorescence
        image = dataset.read_image(index, contrast_type='fluor', channel=fluor_channel).astype(np.float32)

        yy, xx = np.meshgrid(np.arange(image.shape[0]), np.arange(image.shape[0]))
        fluor_mask = np.sqrt((yy - image.shape[0]/2) ** 2 + (xx - image.shape[1]/2) ** 2) < image.shape[0]/2
        fluor_mask_pixels = image[fluor_mask]
        fluor_background_pixels = image[np.logical_not(fluor_mask)]
        
        total_fluor = np.mean(fluor_mask_pixels)
        fluor_dataframe.loc[index, fluor_channel + '_total_raw'] = total_fluor
        total_background = np.mean(fluor_background_pixels)
        fluor_dataframe.loc[index, fluor_channel + '_background'] = total_background

import pandas as pd

def compute_spectra(bsccm, channel_names, unmixed_channel_names, single_markers, batch):
    """
    Compute the spectra and brightness of those that will be used for unmixing
    """
    single_marker_unmix_channel_spectra = {}
    single_marker_unmix_channel_brightness = {}
    unmix_channel_spectra = {}
    unmix_channel_brightness = {}
    for name in unmixed_channel_names:
        single_unmix_spectra = []
        for m in single_markers:
            if m in name:
                selection_name = 'selection_example_{}_positive_cells_batch_{}'.format(m, batch)
                spectrum = get_fluor_spectrum(selection_name, bsccm, channel_names)
                single_marker_unmix_channel_spectra[m] = spectrum / np.linalg.norm(spectrum)
                single_marker_unmix_channel_brightness[m] = np.linalg.norm(spectrum)
                single_unmix_spectra.append(spectrum)

        mean_spectra = np.mean(np.stack(single_unmix_spectra, axis=0), axis=0)
        brightness = np.linalg.norm(mean_spectra)
        unmix_channel_spectra[name] = mean_spectra / brightness
        unmix_channel_brightness[name] = brightness
        
    return single_marker_unmix_channel_spectra, single_marker_unmix_channel_brightness, unmix_channel_spectra, unmix_channel_brightness
    

def get_fluor_spectrum(name, bsccm, channel_names):
    """
    Get the spectrum of a particular fluor by looking at difference in median
    between marked and unmarked populations
    """
    marked_indices, non_marked_indices = get_marked_unmarked_indices(name, bsccm)
    non_marked_fluor =  bsccm.surface_marker_dataframe.loc[non_marked_indices, channel_names].to_numpy()
    marked_fluor = bsccm.surface_marker_dataframe.loc[marked_indices, channel_names].to_numpy()
    
#     marked_center = np.percentile(marked_fluor, 95, axis=0) 
#     non_marked_center = np.median(non_marked_fluor, axis=0)
    
    marked_center = np.mean(marked_fluor, axis=0) 
    non_marked_center = np.mean(non_marked_fluor, axis=0)
    
    spectrum =  marked_center - non_marked_center
    spectrum[spectrum < 0] = 0
    return spectrum

def load_mixed_data_subset(mixed_data, antibodies, selections, bsccm, batch=0):
    """
    Load the data of a single antibody (or none for autofluor), along with the mask
    that shows marked populations

    """
    indices = bsccm.get_indices(antibodies='unstained' if antibodies == 'autofluor' else antibodies, batch=batch)
    data = mixed_data[indices]
    #if it has a positively marked population
    name = 'selection_example_{}_positive_cells_batch_{}'.format(antibodies, batch)
    if name in selections[batch]:
        marked_mask = get_marked_mask(name, bsccm)
    else:
        marked_mask = None
    return data, marked_mask

def run_experiment(spectra, spectra_names, bsccm, mixed_data, stain_antibodies, selections, reweighting, l1_reg, scatter_fig, scatter_ax, callback_every=50, path='/home/henry/leukosight_data/demixing_results/'):
    """
    Run a single hyperparameter sweep
    """
    for a in scatter_ax:
        a.clear()
    show_antibodies = [m for m in spectra_names if stain_antibodies in m][0]

    data, mask = load_mixed_data_subset(mixed_data, stain_antibodies, selections, bsccm, batch=0)

    callback = lambda i, loss_history, unmixed: demix_plot_callback(i, loss_history, unmixed, spectra_names, show_antibodies, mask,
                        loss_fig=None, loss_ax=None,
                        scatter_fig=scatter_fig, scatter_ax=scatter_ax, plot_loss_history=500, log_plots=False)

    unmixed, background_spectrum = do_factorization(data, spectra,
                     l1_reg = l1_reg,
                        momentum=0.9,
                        learning_rate = 1e3,
                        background_learning_rate=1e-1,
                        reweighting=reweighting, 
                        callback_every=callback_every,
                        callback=callback)
    
    
    
    save_name = '{}__{}__{}'.format(stain_antibodies, l1_reg, '-'.join(['{:.2f}'.format(r) for r in reweighting]))
    plt.savefig('{}{}.png'.format(path, save_name), transparent=True)

def show_experiment_results(path = '/home/henry/leukosight_data/demixing_results/'):
    """
    Show interactive GUI for viewing the results of hyperparameter sweep experiments
    """
    files = {}
    ab_options = set()
    reg_options = set()
    reweight_options = set()

    for file in os.listdir(path):
        antibody, reg, reweight = file[:-4].split('__')

    #     reweight = (float(r) for r in reweight.split('-'))

        reg_options.add(reg)
        reweight_options.add(reweight)

        files[antibody][reg][reweight] = path + file

        except:

    reweight_dropdown.observe(dropdown_callback, names='value')    

    display(widgets.HBox([antibody_dropdown, reg_dropdown, reweight_dropdown]))

    dropdown_callback(None)

def do_factorization(data, spectra, l1_reg = 1e0,
                    momentum=0.9,
                    learning_rate = 1e3,
                    background_learning_rate = 1e-1,
                    background_reg = 5e-2,
                    reweighting = jnp.ones(6), 
                     callback_every=50,
                     callback=None,
                    scatter_fig=None,
                    scatter_ax=None,
                    stopping_error=0.0005):
    """
    Do NNMF with given spectra a a fixed background
    """
    if data.size == 0:
        raise Exception('Empty data')

    def forward_model(unmixed, background_ones, background_spectrum, reweighting, spectra):    
        mixed = jnp.dot(jnp.concatenate([unmixed, background_ones], axis=1),
                        jnp.concatenate([spectra, background_spectrum], axis=0))

        loss = jnp.mean((data - mixed)**2)
        reweighted = jnp.concatenate([unmixed[:, i] * reweighting[i] for i in range(spectra.shape[0])], axis=-1)

        regularization = 0
        if l1_reg != 0:
            regularization += l1_reg * jnp.mean(jnp.abs(reweighted)) 
            regularization += background_reg * jnp.sum(background_spectrum ** 2)

        return loss + regularization 

    val_grad_fn = jit(value_and_grad(forward_model, [0, 2]))

    target = jnp.array(data)
    unmixed = jnp.ones((data.shape[0], spectra.shape[0]))
    background_ones = jnp.ones((unmixed.shape[0], 1))
    spectra = jnp.array(spectra)
    background_spectrum = jnp.ones([1, spectra.shape[1]]) * 1e-2

    loss_history = []
    step = 0
    for i in range(0, int(1e7)):
        loss, (unmixed_grad, background_spectrum_grad) = val_grad_fn(unmixed, background_ones, background_spectrum, reweighting, spectra)
        loss_history.append(loss)

        # take step
        step = momentum * step - learning_rate * unmixed_grad
        unmixed += step

        background_spectrum -= background_learning_rate * background_spectrum_grad 

        #enforce constraints
        unmixed = unmixed * jnp.logical_not(unmixed < 0)
        background_spectrum = background_spectrum * jnp.logical_not(background_spectrum < 0)

        if i > 50:
            rel_error = (np.abs(loss_history[-50] - loss_history[-1]) / loss_history[-1])

def corr(a, b):
    a, b = np.asarray(a), np.asarray(b)
    ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    if ok.sum() < 3 or np.std(a[ok]) == 0 or np.std(b[ok]) == 0:
        return float('nan')
    return float(pearsonr(a[ok], b[ok]).statistic)


def atomic_json(path, obj):
    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + '.tmp')
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\\n')
    tmp.replace(path)


def json_clean(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {str(k): json_clean(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [json_clean(v) for v in obj]
    if isinstance(obj, np.generic):
        return json_clean(obj.item())
    if isinstance(obj, float) and not np.isfinite(obj):
        return None
    return obj

def pixel_chunk(item):
    key, rows = item
    means = np.empty((len(rows), 2, 2, 6), dtype=np.float64)
    quality = np.zeros((len(rows), 2), dtype=np.int64)
    for k, g in enumerate(rows):
        image = np.asarray(FL[int(g)])
        quality[k] = [np.count_nonzero(image == 0), np.count_nonzero(image >= 4095)]
        for h, (fg, bg) in enumerate(PIX):
            means[k, h, 0] = image[:, fg].mean(axis=1, dtype=np.float64)
            means[k, h, 1] = image[:, bg].mean(axis=1, dtype=np.float64)
    return key, rows, means, quality

    for key, rr in chunks:
        p = cache / f'{key:06d}.npz'
        if not p.exists():

    if missing:
        # fork is explicit: Linux container and uv smoke share the same path; no training dependencies.
        with mp.get_context('fork').Pool(workers, initializer=init_worker, initargs=(str(pack),)) as pool:
            for key, rr, means, quality in pool.imap_unordered(pixel_chunk, missing, chunksize=1):
                p = cache / f'{key:06d}.npz'
                tmp = p.with_suffix('.tmp.npz')

                tmp.replace(p)
                if key % 20 == 0:
                    print(f'Checkpoint chunk {key}', flush=True)
                if STOP:
                    pool.terminate()
                    raise SystemExit(143)
    arrays, qq = [], []
    for key, rr in chunks:
        with np.load(cache / f'{key:06d}.npz') as z:

def allocate_smoke(plan, limit, rng):
    if not limit:
        return plan
    strata = list(plan.groupby(['cohort', 'antibodies'], sort=True).indices.values())
    if limit < len(strata) * 3:
        raise ValueError('max-cells must allow at least three rows per cohort x antibody')
    chosen = []
    perm = [rng.permutation(v) for v in strata]
    for k in itertools.count():
        for v in perm:
            if k < len(v):
                chosen.append(int(v[k]))
                if len(chosen) == min(limit, len(plan)):
                    return plan.iloc[sorted(chosen)].reset_index(drop=True)


def make_plan(t, idx, goal, limit, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    records = []
    for direction, test_batch in [('b10', 0), ('b01', 1)]:
        # All masked-in GOAL cells, without additional histology/QC filtering.
        ev = np.flatnonzero((t['split'] == 2) & (t['batch'] == test_batch) & t['mask'][:, goal].any(1))
        for g in ev:
            records.append((int(g), direction, 'eval', idx.antibodies.iloc[g]))
        for ab, count in pd.Series(idx.antibodies.values[ev]).value_counts().items():
            candidates = np.flatnonzero((t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0) &
                                       (t['batch'] == 1-test_batch) & (idx.antibodies.values == ab) &
                                       t['mask'][:, goal].any(1))
            selected = rng.choice(candidates, min(count, len(candidates)), replace=False)
            for g in selected:
                records.append((int(g), direction, 'train_matched', ab))
    plan = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=['G', 'direction', 'role', 'antibodies'])
    plan['cohort'] = plan.direction + ':' + plan.role
    plan = allocate_smoke(plan, limit, rng)
    # Each draw's split-0 rows occur in one training cohort, split-2 in one eval cohort.
    assert plan.G.is_unique
    return plan.sort_values('G').reset_index(drop=True)


def qp_unmix(x, spectra, offset, floors):
    \"\"\"Exact 4-component nonnegative quadratic optimum by enumerating 16 active sets.\"\"\"
    hess = spectra @ spectra.T
    q = x @ spectra.T - offset
    best = np.full(len(x), np.inf)
    ans = np.zeros_like(q)
    for bits in range(16):
        active = np.flatnonzero([(bits >> j) & 1 for j in range(4)])
        a = np.zeros_like(q)
        if len(active):
            a[:, active] = q[:, active] @ np.linalg.inv(hess[np.ix_(active, active)])
        valid = (a >= -1e-8).all(axis=1)
        objective = .5 * np.sum((a @ hess) * a, axis=1) - np.sum(a*q, axis=1)
        take = valid & (objective < best)
        ans[take], best[take] = a[take], objective[take]
    assert np.isfinite(best).all()
    return np.maximum(ans, floors)


def pool_model(sm, idx, t, batch, condition, corrected, raw):
    \"\"\"Frozen authors' gate spectra; recover nuisance gradient offset on clean split-0 only.

    Authors' nonnegative L1 unmixing with fixed spectra has a quadratic KKT system.
    The offset absorbs their fitted condition background, positive channel shift and L1.
    Recovery is approximate because the released iterative solver stopped early.
    \"\"\"
    spectra = []
    for group in GROUPS:
        components = []
        for marker in group.split('/'):
            gate = sm[f'selection_example_{marker}_positive_cells_batch_{batch}'].values.astype(bool)
            first = np.flatnonzero(gate)[0]
            ref = ((idx.antibodies.values == idx.antibodies.iloc[first]) &
                   (idx.batch.values == batch) &
                   (idx.slide_replicate.values == idx.slide_replicate.iloc[first]) & ~gate)
            # These are the authors' frozen spectrum gates, not a fit to evaluation outcomes.
            components.append(np.maximum(0, corrected[gate].mean(0) - corrected[ref].mean(0)))
        v = np.mean(components, axis=0)
        spectra.append(v / np.linalg.norm(v))
    spectra = np.asarray(spectra)
    cal = (t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0) & (t['batch'] == batch)
    tr = cal & (idx.antibodies.values == condition)
    floors = np.nanmin(raw[cal], axis=0)
    active = raw > floors * (1 + 1e-6)
    a = np.where(active, raw, 0)
    residual = corrected @ spectra.T - a @ (spectra @ spectra.T)
    offset = []
    for j in range(4):
        rr = tr & active[:, j]
        if rr.sum() < 20:
            raise ValueError(f'Insufficient uncensored pooled calibration: {batch}/{condition}/{j}')
        offset.append(np.median(residual[rr, j]))
    return dict(spectra=spectra.tolist(), offset=offset, floors=floors.tolist())


def apply_pool(x, model):
    return qp_unmix(x, np.asarray(model['spectra']), np.asarray(model['offset']), np.asarray(model['floors']))


def curate(raw, rows, j, t, sm, keep_trend=False):
    \"\"\"v3 cofactor/clean-split-0 z, frozen xfit correction, frozen v5 slide normalisation.\"\"\"
    name = str(t['names'][j])
    y = np.full(len(rows), np.nan)
    for b in (0, 1):
        loc = t['batch'][rows] == b
        cal = (t['batch'] == b) & (t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0)
        measured = t['mask'][:, j]
        if name.startswith('single:'):
            marker = name.split(':', 1)[1]
            original = sm[f'{marker}_single_antibody_model_unmixed'].values
            transformed = np.arcsinh(original[cal & measured] / COF[marker])
            v = np.arcsinh(raw[loc] / COF[marker])
        else:
            group = name.split(':', 1)[1]
            original = sm[f'{group}_full_model_unmixed'].values
            ref = cal & ~t['stained']
            med = np.median(original[ref])
            mad = np.median(np.abs(original[ref] - med))*1.4826 + 1e-6
            transformed = np.arcsinh((original[cal & measured] - med)/mad)
            v = np.arcsinh((raw[loc] - med)/mad)
        y[loc] = (v - transformed.mean()) / (transformed.std() + 1e-6)
    if not keep_trend:
        y -= (t['Y_v3'][rows, j] - t['Y_v4'][rows, j])
    if name.startswith('grp:'):
        for b in (0, 1):
            sel = t['mask'][:, j] & (t['batch'] == b)
            slides = np.unique(t['slide'][sel])
            if len(slides) < 2:
                continue
            cal = sel & (t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0)
            stats = {}
            ref_parts = []
            for slide in slides:
                a = t['Y_v4'][cal & (t['slide'] == slide), j].astype(np.float64)
                q1, med, q3 = np.percentile(a, [25, 50, 75])
                scale = max((q3-q1)/1.349, 1e-6)
                stats[int(slide)] = (med, scale)
                ref_parts.append((a-med)/scale)
            ref = np.concatenate(ref_parts)
            for slide, (med, scale) in stats.items():
                loc = (t['batch'][rows] == b) & (t['slide'][rows] == slide)
                y[loc] = ((y[loc]-med)/scale-ref.mean())/ref.std()
    return y


def reliability(a, b):
    r = corr(a, b)
    rho = 2*r/(1+r) if np.isfinite(r) and r > -1 else float('nan')
    rmax = np.sqrt(rho) if np.isfinite(rho) and 0 <= rho <= 1 else float('nan')
    return r, rho, rmax


def fov_decomposition(y, p, fov):
    e = y-p
    _, inverse = np.unique(fov, return_inverse=True)
    n = np.bincount(inverse)
    means = np.bincount(inverse, weights=e)/n
    total = float(np.var(e))
    between = float(np.average((means-e.mean())**2, weights=n))
    within = float(np.mean((e-means[inverse])**2))
    assert np.isclose(total, between+within)
    # ANOVA random-intercept sensitivity; all FOVs including singleton groups contribute.
    nf, nc = len(n), len(e)
    msw = float(np.sum((e-means[inverse])**2)/(nc-nf)) if nc > nf else float('nan')
    msb = float(np.sum(n*(means-e.mean())**2)/(nf-1)) if nf > 1 else float('nan')
    n0 = (nc - np.sum(n*n)/nc)/(nf-1) if nf > 1 else float('nan')
    component = max(0., (msb-msw)/n0) if np.isfinite(msw+msb+n0) else float('nan')
    return dict(n=nc, n_fov=nf, singleton_fov=int((n == 1).sum()), residual_variance=total,
                variance_fov_means_unweighted=float(np.var(means)), between_variance_weighted=between,
                within_variance=within, fov_share=between/total if total else float('nan'),
                finite_n_null_share=(nf-1)/(nc-1) if nc > 1 else float('nan'),
                anova_fov_component=component, anova_share=component/(component+msw) if component+msw > 0 else float('nan'))


def predictions(source, direction, expected):
    result = []
    for arm in ('n048_v9_base', 'n048_v9_zoom2', 'n053_cytoland'):
        with np.load(source / 'runs' / f'{arm}_{direction}' / 'eval_preds.npz') as e:

def md_table(frame, columns=None):

def main():

    maps = json.loads(args.maps.read_text())['models']

def qp_unmix(x, spectra, offset, floors):
    \"\"\"Exact 4-component nonnegative quadratic optimum by enumerating 16 active sets.\"\"\"
    hess = spectra @ spectra.T
    q = x @ spectra.T - offset
    best = np.full(len(x), np.inf)
    ans = np.zeros_like(q)
    for bits in range(16):
        active = np.flatnonzero([(bits >> j) & 1 for j in range(4)])
        a = np.zeros_like(q)
        if len(active):
            a[:, active] = q[:, active] @ np.linalg.inv(hess[np.ix_(active, active)])
        valid = (a >= -1e-8).all(axis=1)
        objective = .5 * np.sum((a @ hess) * a, axis=1) - np.sum(a*q, axis=1)
        take = valid & (objective < best)
        ans[take], best[take] = a[take], objective[take]
    assert np.isfinite(best).all()
    return np.maximum(ans, floors)


def pool_model(sm, idx, t, batch, condition, corrected, raw):
    \"\"\"Frozen authors' gate spectra; recover nuisance gradient offset on clean split-0 only.

    Recovery is approximate because the released iterative solver stopped early.

            components.append(np.maximum(0, corrected[gate].mean(0) - corrected[ref].mean(0)))
        v = np.mean(components, axis=0)
        spectra.append(v / np.linalg.norm(v))

    tr = cal & (idx.antibodies.values == condition)

    for j in range(4):
        rr = tr & active[:, j]
        if rr.sum() < 20:
            raise ValueError(f'Insufficient uncensored pooled calibration: {batch}/{condition}/{j}')
        offset.append(np.median(residual[rr, j]))
    return dict(spectra=spectra.tolist(), offset=offset, floors=floors.tolist())


def apply_pool(x, model):
    return qp_unmix(x, np.asarray(model['spectra']), np.asarray(model['offset']), np.asarray(model['floors']))


def curate(raw, rows, j, t, sm, keep_trend=False):
    \"\"\"v3 cofactor/clean-split-0 z, frozen xfit correction, frozen v5 slide normalisation.\"\"\"
    name = str(t['names'][j])
    y = np.full(len(rows), np.nan)
    for b in (0, 1):
        loc = t['batch'][rows] == b
        cal = (t['batch'] == b) & (t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0)
        measured = t['mask'][:, j]
        if name.startswith('single:'):
            marker = name.split(':', 1)[1]
            original = sm[f'{marker}_single_antibody_model_unmixed'].values
            transformed = np.arcsinh(original[cal & measured] / COF[marker])
            v = np.arcsinh(raw[loc] / COF[marker])
        else:
            group = name.split(':', 1)[1]
            original = sm[f'{group}_full_model_unmixed'].values
            ref = cal & ~t['stained']
            med = np.median(original[ref])
            mad = np.median(np.abs(original[ref] - med))*1.4826 + 1e-6
            transformed = np.arcsinh((original[cal & measured] - med)/mad)
            v = np.arcsinh((raw[loc] - med)/mad)
        y[loc] = (v - transformed.mean()) / (transformed.std() + 1e-6)
    if not keep_trend:
        y -= (t['Y_v3'][rows, j] - t['Y_v4'][rows, j])
    if name.startswith('grp:'):
        for b in (0, 1):
            sel = t['mask'][:, j] & (t['batch'] == b)
            slides = np.unique(t['slide'][sel])
            if len(slides) < 2:
                continue
            cal = sel & (t['split'] == 0) & (t['hist_row'] < 0)
            stats = {}
            ref_parts = []
            for slide in slides:
                a = t['Y_v4'][cal & (t['slide'] == slide), j].astype(np.float64)
                q1, med, q3 = np.percentile(a, [25, 50, 75])
                scale = max((q3-q1)/1.349, 1e-6)
                stats[int(slide)] = (med, scale)
                ref_parts.append((a-med)/scale)
            ref = np.concatenate(ref_parts)
            for slide, (med, scale) in stats.items():
                loc = (t['batch'][rows] == b) & (t['slide'][rows] == slide)
                y[loc] = ((y[loc]-med)/scale-ref.mean())/ref.std()
    return y


def reliability(a, b):
    r = corr(a, b)
    rho = 2*r/(1+r) if np.isfinite(r) and r > -1 else float('nan')
    rmax = np.sqrt(rho) if np.isfinite(rho) and 0 <= rho <= 1 else float('nan')
    return r, rho, rmax


def fov_decomposition(y, p, fov):
    e = y-p
    _, inverse = np.unique(fov, return_inverse=True)
    n = np.bincount(inverse)
    means = np.bincount(inverse, weights=e)/n
    total = float(np.var(e))
    between = float(np.average((means-e.mean())**2, weights=n))
    within = float(np.mean((e-means[inverse])**2))
    assert np.isclose(total, between+within)
    # ANOVA random-intercept sensitivity; all FOVs including singleton groups contribute.
    nf, nc = len(n), len(e)
    msw = float(np.sum((e-means[inverse])**2)/(nc-nf)) if nc > nf else float('nan')
    msb = float(np.sum(n*(means-e.mean())**2)/(nf-1)) if nf > 1 else float('nan')
    n0 = (nc - np.sum(n*n)/nc)/(nf-1) if nf > 1 else float('nan')
    component = max(0., (msb-msw)/n0) if np.isfinite(msw+msb+n0) else float('nan')
    return dict(n=nc, n_fov=nf, singleton_fov=int((n == 1).sum()), residual_variance=total,
                variance_fov_means_unweighted=float(np.var(means)), between_variance_weighted=between,
                within_variance=within, fov_share=between/total if total else float('nan'),
                finite_n_null_share=(nf-1)/(nc-1) if nc > 1 else float('nan'),
                anova_fov_component=component, anova_share=component/(component+msw) if component+msw > 0 else float('nan'))


def predictions(source, direction, expected):
    result = []
    for arm in ('n048_v9_base', 'n048_v9_zoom2', 'n053_cytoland'):
        with np.load(source / 'runs' / f'{arm}_{direction}' / 'eval_preds.npz') as e:
            g, p = e['G'], e['P']
        if len(np.unique(g)) "'!= len(g):
            raise ValueError(f'"'Duplicate prediction G in {arm}/{direction}')
        lookup = pd.Index(g).get_indexer(expected)
        if (lookup < 0).any():
            raise ValueError(f'Missing GOAL rows in {arm}/{direction}')
        result.append(p[lookup])
    return np.mean(result, axis=0)


def md_table(frame, columns=None):
    if columns is not None:
        frame = frame[columns]
    # No tabulate dependency in the training container.
    fmt = lambda v: f'{v:.5f}' if isinstance(v, (float, np.floating)) else str(v)
    return '| ' + ' | '.join(frame.columns) + ' |\\n| ' + ' | '.join(['---']*len(frame.columns)) + ' |\\n' + '\\n'.join('| ' + ' | '.join(fmt(v) for v in row) + ' |' for row in frame.itertuples(index=False, name=None)) + '\\n'
